payload.title: Falsify ActiveAssembly conflict-budget scheduling on frozen H1 traces
payload.work_clay: Run matched fixed-context ActiveAssembly selection trials that vary conflict density and evidence ancestry. Compare current unconditional conflict-first selection against broad retrieval/cache, diversity-aware ranking, claim-group compression, fixed conflict reservation and adaptive utility-aware conflict allocation. Preserve unresolved contradictions and re-expansion references; never let cognitive selection mint effect authority.
payload.reason_clay: EXP-FRANK-AA-CONFLICT-BUDGET-001 found a deterministic starvation counterexample: four two-way conflict groups can consume all eight current Assembly slots and exclude three higher-score non-conflict packets. A 10,000-trial authored synthetic sweep showed a strong conflict-visibility versus critical-retention tradeoff, but cannot select a production quota because the task-critical labels were authored.
payload.completion_clay: Use frozen H1/Golden Trace episodes or later live target-Ubuntu traces. Sweep conflict cardinality, context budget and ancestry duplication. Measure verified task outcome, explicit contradiction recall, provenance/ancestry fidelity, omitted-detail re-expansion success, false certainty, correction time, token/KV use, selection latency, update amplification and downstream GWT/4B causal use. Accept a changed policy only if it improves the matched quality/cost vector without hiding material contradictions; otherwise retain current policy or a simpler retrieval baseline.
dependencies: H1 frozen/Golden Trace corpus with groundable task outcomes
stable semantic/provenance/claim identity from H-WP-02 state-ledger convergence
invalidators: newer executable evidence already resolves ActiveAssembly conflict allocation
ActiveAssembly is superseded by a simpler retrieval/cache mechanism after matched H1 evidence
